title: character count brevity or legal
rule: Character count only for brevity or a legal cap — not to paper over backend field limits (raise the limit). Skip if length is implied (phone/zip) or if well over 99% of users will never hit the cap (e.g. address at 250). Provide a non-JS backup message. Dual-cite GOV.UK raise-backend + no-maxlength-truncate vs USWDS using `maxlength` for the component. No winner on truncate.
pass_when: Count is shown only for brevity or a legal cap; backend limit is raised rather than used as a fake cap; implied-length and never-hit caps omit the count; a non-JS backup message exists.
fail_when: Count papers over a short backend limit; or count on phone/zip / an address field almost nobody will hit.
overview: Show character count only for brevity or a legal cap, not to paper over a short backend limit.
apply_when: Textareas with a real brevity need or legal maximum users might hit.
not_when: Phone/zip implied lengths, or caps almost nobody will hit such as address at 250.
agent_hint: Use character count only for brevity or legal caps; raise backend limits instead of faking them.
description: USWDS character count is for brevity or a legal cap—not to paper over backend field limits (raise the limit instead). Skip when length is implied (phone/zip) or when well over 99% of users will never hit the cap. Provide a non-JS backup message. Dual-cite GOV.UK raise-backend and no-maxlength-truncate versus USWDS `maxlength` usage without picking a truncate winner. Counting to hide a short backend limit, or counting phone/zip/rarely-hit address fields, fails.
do_not_claim: A winner that bans or requires `maxlength`.
